required_outcomes: Links the mould to the 10 Oct leak and notices that the drying-out recommended on the job sheet was never arranged before R-4830 was closed.
Raises a new job (or reopens R-4830) for drying out, a damp and mould inspection and the swollen sink unit base, and arranges a visit with the tenant's consent.
Informs the landlord that the leak's aftermath needs work, and that it may form part of the insurance claim already flagged.
Replies to the tenant with practical interim advice (ventilate, heat, report any spread) without blaming her or treating it as a lifestyle issue.
acceptable_alternatives: Supplying a dehumidifier straight away while the inspection is arranged.
Routing the rent question to the right team or answering that no increase has been notified, without guessing.
positive_behaviours: Acknowledges that the follow-up was missed.
Asks for photos of the mould and the unit for the record and the insurer.
red_flags: Treats the mould as condensation from the tenant's lifestyle.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant to treat it herself and closing the matter.
Inventing a rent increase figure or date.
critical_failures: Taking no action on the damp and mould.
